audit.why: 50.08% over 645 games — an even matchup that is really two lanes: a free ranged poke window against a dashless mage before 6, then a drain-tank who out-sustains you after it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chart reads Skill|Jayce|Jayce|Skill|Skill|Jayce|Jayce, yet whys[0] says you 'chip him for free' at level 1, spikes[1] calls level 6 'Swain's spike, not yours', spikes[2] says first item 'flattens toward even', and late says 'This is Swain's game if it gets here'.
audit.why: The chart gives Jayce both item stages the text hands to Swain, and calls level 1 even when the text calls it free. Packet reference chart Jayce|Jayce|Jayce|Skill|Swain|Skill|Swain matches the prose exactly.
audit.corrected: Sides re-set to Jayce, Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Swain, Skill, Swain.

audit.whatIsWrong: early calls Nevermove 'a delayed skillshot root'. Riot's text: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The root is on the RETURN pass, not the outgoing one.
audit.why: This is the single most misplayed thing in the matchup and it decides your poke rhythm. The outbound wave is free to stand in; the dangerous instant is after it has gone past you and is coming back. Telling a player to 'dodge the skillshot' aims them at the wrong half of the ability.
audit.corrected: early now says it roots on the return and to clear the path back.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal call anywhere despite Swain being a healing champion at every stage.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock (P) heals him off soul fragments and permanently raises his max health, and Demonic Ascension drains from everything nearby for 120 seconds of cooldown. Grievous Wounds timing is the decision that makes a post-6 fight possible.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds and the 120s R stated in mid.

audit.why: Nevermove 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s (and shorter during Demonic Ascension), Vision of Empire 22/21/20/19/18s, Death's Hand only 7s, Demonic Ascension 120s. The 12s E is the window you commit in.

edits.before: Your accelerated gate-Q is the whole early game here — Swain is a slow, dashless drain-mage who must walk up to farm, so fire Shock Blast through your E gate and detonate it on him every time he steps to last-hit. At level 2-3, poke with Cannon-Q then swap to Hammer so the first attack shreds his armor/MR, and follow with the Q-E-W combo for a real chunk. The one thing to respect is his E, Nevermove: it's a delayed skillshot root, and if it lands his passive yanks you toward him for his W and Q, so dodge it and poke at max gate range instead of standing in his face.
edits.after: Your accelerated gate-Q is the whole early game here — Swain is a slow, dashless drain-mage who must walk up to farm, so fire Shock Blast through your E gate and detonate it on him every time he steps to last-hit. At level 2-3, poke with Cannon-Q then swap to Hammer so the first attack shreds his armor/MR, and follow with the Q-E-W combo for a real chunk. Respect his E, Nevermove: the outgoing wave does nothing — it roots on the RETURN pass, so the dangerous instant is after it has gone by you. Clear the way back and poke at max gate range.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you're still ahead in the poke war — keep banking his health bar with accelerated orbs while he has no real way to heal it back yet. Level 6 is the flip: his Demonic Ascension is a genuine spike where your R is only the stance-swap you already had, so the moment he ults, do NOT keep brawling — he drains through your damage and grows the longer the fight runs. Trade strictly while his R is down, knock him away with Thundering Blow if he walks you down, and swap to Cannon to re-poke from range.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you're still ahead in the poke war — bank his health bar with accelerated orbs while his only healing is soul fragments. Level 6 is the flip: Demonic Ascension is a genuine spike on a 120s cooldown where your R is only the stance-swap, so the moment he ults, do NOT keep brawling — he drains through your damage and grows the longer it runs. Ravenous Flock heals him and stacks permanent HP, so Grievous Wounds is a real buy here. Trade while his 12s Nevermove is down, knock him off with Thundering Blow, and swap to Cannon to re-poke.

edits.before: Land E (Nevermove) root so his passive pulls you in and his W and Q land on a stationary Jayce
edits.after: Catch you with the RETURN half of Nevermove (E), then pull you in so W and Q land on a stationary Jayce

notes: Nevermove roots on the wave's return trip, not the outbound cast — the page framed it as a single delayed skillshot, which points the player at the wrong half. Swain was flagged for missing anti-heal in _missing-interactions.json and had no Grievous Wounds line anywhere; added to mid.
